title: LEAN NO MORE A: Cognitive Niche Differentiation of Formalization Tools– Theoretical Foundations of a Polycentric Governance Architecture
abstract: The formal verification community is currently undergoing a covert cognitivemonopoly: a single tool, by virtue of its industrial maturity and community size,is rapidly occupying a supercritical market share, leading to a sharp contractionof logical diversity within the formalization ecosystem. This paper reexamines theproper relationship among proof assistants from the perspective of cognitive nichetheory. The core argument is that different proof assistants, owing to differencesin their underlying logical foundations, should occupy functionally differentiatedcognitive niches rather than substituting for each other under the banner of “generality”. On the theoretical level, we establish a four-dimensional characterizationmodel for the cognitive niches of formalization tools– verification depth, structural openness, equality granularity, and generative capacity– and accordinglyclassify existing tools into three niche types: verification-oriented, constructionoriented, and synthesis-oriented. We further introduce niche construction theoryto reveal the reverse-shaping effect of tools on mathematical practice, demonstrating that this effect, together with network externalities, constitutes an irreversiblecognitive lock-in. On the dynamical level, we introduce a multi-market replicatormodel with niche construction feedback to analyze technological path evolution,prove that without external intervention the system necessarily converges to asingle tool, and provide quantitative conditions for the switching cost thresholdand the intervention window. On the governance level, we propose a cognitive diversity regularization mechanism based on niche differentiation, including dynamically protected observation periods, niche-specific triggering conditions for forklegitimacy, differentiated weights for cross-verification incentives, and institutionalpatches compatible with current academic evaluation systems. On the engineeringlevel, we design weak-loyalty translation functors for polycentric architectures, layered bridging protocols with niche-distance awareness, distributed meta-auditingmechanisms, and a coordination game analysis for standardization adoption. Finally, we propose a health indicator system for the formalization ecosystem, arguefor an optimal interval of cognitive diversity, and point out that the long-termhealth of the formalization ecosystem does not depend on the technical perfectionof any single tool, but on the anti-fragility of the entire system along the dimensionof logical diversity.

title: KAM RESURSLI TILLARNI RAQAMLASHTIRISHDA SUN‘IY INTELLEKT MODELLARINING SAMARADORLIGI VA MAVJUD MUAMMOLAR
abstract: Ushbu maqolada kam resursli tillar, xususan, qoraqalpoq tili uchun sun’iy intellekt va tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash (NLP) modellarini ishlab chiqishdagi dolzarb muammolar tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotning asosiy maqsadi - ma‘lumotlar tanqisligi sharoitida model aniqligini oshirish uchun ma‘lumotlarni tozalash va normalizatsiya qilish metodikasini ishlab chiqishdir. Bunda qoraqalpoq tili o‘ziga xos harflari uchun maxsus normallashtirish algoritmlari va Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenlashtirishi qo‘llanilgan. Natijalar shuni ko‘rsatdiki, taklif etilgan preprocessing usullari model xatoligini (Loss) sezilarli darajada kamaytirib, tarjima va qidiruv aniqligini (BLEU score) 12.4 dan 24.8 gacha oshirish imkonini berdi. Tadqiqot xulosalari kam resursli tillar uchun raqamli lug‘atlar va aqlli tizimlar yaratishda nazariy va amaliy asos bo‘lib xizmat qiladi.

title: Introduction to Firmware Reverse Engineering for IoT Devices Using Ghidra and Binwalk
abstract: The fast usage of Internet of Things (IoT) device in industrial and consumer settings has dramatically expanded on the attack surface of embedded systems. This paper explores firmware security through reverse engineering and analysis of a firmware image of an IoT style with two open-source tools: Binwalk and Ghidra. An artificial representation of the structure of typical Linux-based IoT firmware was produced by a controlled firmware image which had a SquashFS file system and compiled binaries. Embedded file systems and binaries were extracted using Binwalk and Ghidra was used to do the static analysis and decompilation of extracted executable files. The vulnerability analysis showed that there are a number of deliberately introduced security flaws such as hard-coded credentials, unsecured input handling functions and insecure configuration practices. The success of the method was shown by the successful recovery of the firmware filesystem and detection of these types of vulnerabilities with the help of the strict reverse-engineering tool. The paper shows the possible contribution of open-source tools to the analysis of firmware-level vulnerabilities and enhancing security testing of embedded IoT systems.

title: Comparing acoustic cues to phrase boundary in Hindi and Indian English
abstract: Prosody is key to spoken language communication, integral to conveying meaning, emotion and emphasis beyond the literal speech.While several languages share the linguistic elements of phrase boundary and prominence, their acoustic realizations can vary considerably.With the goal to investigate whether languages can be discriminated based purely on prosody, we carry out a perception experiment with delexicalised speech of Hindi and Indian English model readers.With Hindi surpassing English, the overall language recognition accuracy was 63.5%, with highest individual listener accuracy of 79.0%.Acoustic cues at boundaries were examined across languages via word level features related to f0, intensity, duration and pause.Intensity features were crucial indicators of different boundary types in Hindi while duration based cues dominated automatic boundary classification in English.

title: Eliminating reversals from cubical type theories
abstract: Cubical type theories are designed around an abstract unit interval from which types of paths, used to represent equalities, are defined. Varying the operations available on this interval yields different type theories. A reversal is an involutive operator on the interval that swaps its two endpoints. We show that for cubical type theories with self-dual interval theories, such as the minimal theory of two endpoints or the theory of a bounded distributive lattice, the extension of the theory with a reversal that internalizes the duality is a conservative extension. The key tool is a "twist construction": the product of an interval and its dual is again an interval with a reversal given by swapping coordinates. Our conservativity result applies to "opaque" cubical type theories, without strict equations reducing the filling operator at concrete type formers or eliminators from higher inductive types at path constructors. Using the same twist construction, we also construct models of strict cubical type theory with reversals in categories of cubical sets without reversals. We thereby give the first model of a theory with reversals whose homotopy theory corresponds to that of topological spaces.

title: Emotion-Attended Stateful Memory (EASM):The Architecture for Hyper-Personalization at Scale
abstract: Current language model systems remain fundamentally stateless across sessions, limiting their ability to personalize interactions over time. While retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning improve knowledge access and domain capability, they do not enable persistent understanding of individual users. We propose an emotion-attended stateful memory architecture that dynamically constructs user-specific conversational context using long-term history, emotional signals, and inferred intent at inference time. To evaluate its impact, we conducted a controlled A/B study across thirty non-scripted conversations spanning six emotionally distinct categories using the same underlying language model in both conditions. The memory-enriched condition consistently outperformed the stateless baseline across all evaluated scenarios. The largest gains were observed in memory grounding (95% improvement), plan clarity (57%), and emotional validation (34%). Results remained consistent even in emotionally adversarial conversations involving grief, distress, and uncertainty. These findings suggest that stateful emotional memory may represent a foundational infrastructure layer for hyper-personalized AI systems, though broader validation across larger and more diverse evaluations remains necessary

We propose an emotion-attended stateful memory architecture that dynamically constructs user-specific conversational context using long-term history, emotional signals, and inferred intent at inference time. To evaluate its impact, we conducted a controlled A/B study across thirty non-scripted conversations spanning six emotionally distinct categories using the same underlying language model in both conditions. The memory-enriched condition consistently outperformed the stateless baseline across all evaluated scenarios. The largest gains were observed in memory grounding (95% improvement), plan clarity (57%), and emotional validation (34%). Results remained consistent even in emotionally adversarial conversations involving grief, distress, and uncertainty. These findings suggest that stateful emotional memory may represent a foundational infrastructure layer for hyper-personalized AI systems, though broader validation across larger and more diverse evaluations remains necessary

title: Modeling the impact of artificial intelligence recommendations on purchase intentions for smart devices and their accessories
abstract: Šiuolaikinėje el. prekybos aplinkoje vartotojų sprendimų priėmimo procesas vis labiau siejamas su dirbtinio intelekto įrankiais, vis daugiau naudojamasi generatyvinio dirbtinio intelekto pokalbių agentais ir paieškos sistemose pateikiamomis dirbtinio intelekto sugeneruotomis apžvalgomis. Tokios rekomendacijos gali tapti vienu pirmųjų vartotojo sąlyčio taškų su produktu ar pardavėju, todėl svarbu suprasti, kokie tokių rekomendacijų aspektai gali paveikti vartotojo pirkimo ketinimus. Šio darbo tyrimo problema – kaip sumodeliuoti generatyvinio dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijų poveikį vartotojų pirkimo ketinimams išmaniųjų įrenginių ir jų priedų kategorijoje. Šio darbo objektas – dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijų poveikis pirkimo ketinimams. Darbo tikslas – empiriškai patvirtinus teorinį dirbtinio intelekto generatyvių rekomendacijų poveikio vartotojų pirkimo ketinimams modelį išmaniųjų įrenginių ir jų priedų produktų atveju, atlikti mokslinę diskusiją bei pateikti modelio taikymo galimybes ir apribojimus. Tyrimo metodai: mokslinės literatūros analizė, anketinė apklausa, ekspertų interviu. Remiantis teorine analize buvo sudarytas teorinis generatyvinio dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijų poveikio vartotojų pirkimo ketinimams modelis. Modeliui pagrįsti iškelti 9 tiriamieji teiginiai siekiant įvertinti, ar suvokiama dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijų informacijos kokybė, suvokiama vartotojo sąveikos su dirbtiniu intelektu kokybė ir rekomendacijų skaidrumas veikia vartotojo pasitikėjimą, suvokiamą vertę, o šie veiksniai daro poveikį pirkimo ketinimui. Taip pat modelyje vertinama, ar privatumo rizika turi moderacinį poveikį pasitikėjimo dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijomis ir pirkimo ketinimo ryšiui. Pagrindinės darbo išvados: kiekybinio tyrimo rezultatai (393 respondentai) parodė, kad pirkimo ketinimą reikšmingai veikia pasitikėjimas dirbtinio intelekto rekomendacijomis, suvokiama utilitarinė vertė ir suvokiama hedoninė vertė. Iš viso patvirtinti aštuoni tiriamieji teiginiai, o teiginys dėl privatumo rizikos moderaciniu poveikiu iš dalies patvirtintas.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Similarity Measures for Semi-Supervised Density Peaks Clustering
abstract: Semi-supervised Density Peak (SDenPeak) algorithm is known to be efficient and simple in tasks clustering. It improves clustering performance by adding pair-wise constraints, must-link and cannot-link constraints, that drive the grouping process by imposing similarity and dissimilarity between data points. One of the key considerations in clustering accuracy is the selection of similarity measure because various measures reflect diverse structural attributes to data. The problem with the fact that there is no universal best measure of similarity is that it is a tricky task to choose a suitable measure that is dependent on the nature of the data. To explore the effects of the six similarity measures on SDenPeak algorithm performance, the six measures (Euclidean Distance, Cosine Similarity, City Block (Manhattan) Distance, Minkowski Distance, Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD), and Rapid Computation of the Maximal Information Coefficient (RapidMIC) Distance) are evaluated systematically in this study in order to understand their influences Real-world datasets are extensively experimented to evaluate the accuracy of clustering and structural consistency in each of the measures. These findings present comparative information on the effectiveness of the various similarity measures and illustrate their applicability to various data distributions providing a useful guide to achieving the best clustering performance in semi-supervised models.

title: Q/K/V Sign Taxonomy: A Forward-Only Universal Head Classifier and Its Applications Across Architectures
abstract: We present a forward-only universal classifier of attention heads: every head in any transformer with linear Q/K/V projections (decoder or encoder, absolute or rotary positional encoding, 144 to 720+ heads) is labeled into one of 23 = 8 categories from a fixed template and-slot probe set (N=5 in our experiments; the protocol generalizes to any template-and-slot probe). The procedure requires no training, no gradients, no behavioral intervention, and no learned parameters beyond the model itself. Prior approaches classify heads through behavioral observation [16, 11, 17, 7, 4, 15], gradient-based importance [9], learned soft-gates [10], or output-norm scoring [13]—all of which require backward passes, learned weights, or task specific calibration, and most of which classify only a subset of heads relevant to a particulartask. Our classifier covers 100% of heads from static weight projections alone. We verify the classifier on four models (GPT-2 small/large, BERT-base, Pythia-1.4B) and demonstrate three actionable consequences: (1) per-head measurements predict single-layer-skip perplexity drift with correlation r = +0.73 to +0.87, (2) framework-identified responsible heads can be surgically V-zeroed with 2× to 236,000× less PPL disruption than the corresponding full-layer skip, verified across 3 models and 9 diverse inputs, and (3) the static signature predicts the behavioralfacilitating/interfering/irrelevant label of Nam et al. [10] significantly above chance (χ2 = 26.69,df = 14, p < 0.01). As a direct production application, the framework guides a hybrid pruning pipeline that removes 35% of the KV cache V slice on GPT-2 small with < +1 PPL drift, where random ordering produces catastrophic cumulative damage well before this fraction. We also report a clarifying negative result: the same signal does not predict mixed-precision quantization budget allocation, drawing a sharp boundary on the framework’s predictive utility (removal axis yes, precision axis no). Distribution profiles measured by the classifier differ systematically across training methodologies (GPT-2 vs. BERT vs. Pythia), supporting a stronger reframing of “cross-architecture invariance”—the classifier is universally applicable, and the resulting distribution is a training- methodology fingerprint, not a constant.

title: TLDChoiceNet: Quantitatively Choosing a Transfer Learning Dataset
abstract: TLDChoiceNet introduces a novel deep learning framework for automatically selecting the optimal transfer learning dataset for image classification tasks. The paper explores transfer learning, representation learning, dataset similarity, and neural network feature embeddings by predicting downstream fine-tuning performance before expensive training. TLDChoiceNet leverages dataset embeddings, pretrained model activations, PCA reduction, LoRA-inspired compression, and ResNet50 feature extraction to estimate transfer learning effectiveness across multiple datasets. The research further proposes two quantitative metrics — Distribution Distance (DD) and Average Class Correlation (ACC) — to measure dataset similarity and predict transfer learning accuracy in an unsupervised manner. By analyzing latent feature-space correlations, activation embeddings, and low-level statistical distributions, the framework demonstrates that pretrained representations and dataset statistics strongly influence transfer learning generalization. Experimental results show that TLDChoiceNet v2 achieves a 5× reduction in prediction error over the baseline while ACC achieves a strong correlation (R² = 0.97) with downstream fine-tuning accuracy. This work contributes to machine learning, transfer learning optimization, dataset selection, representation learning, meta-learning, feature similarity analysis, and automated AI model selection, with applications in computer vision, few-shot learning, domain adaptation, and efficient deep learning training pipelines.

title: FigureOut: a lightweight and resilient multi-LLM orchestrator
abstract: FigureOut is a lightweight, modular orchestrator for developers who want to build LLM workflows without the framework bloat. It classifies incoming queries and dispatches them to the appropriate role, returning a structured JSON response. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Meta, Mistral, and Groq with optional MCP tool integration.

title: AI Beneath the Surface
abstract: Artificial Intelligence and its Deep Learning methods are transforming how we detect and locate earthquakes and using traditional Seismological Detection methods often struggles with highly noisy datasets, small-magnitude earthquakes, and human-based feature extraction, whereas Deep Learning models (and specifically Convolutional Neural Networks) allow for the automated analysis of raw seismic waveforms so they can produce higher levels of accuracy and faster and more reliably. This Chapter examines how AI-based Phase Picking, Classifications and Multi-station Source Localisation are changing the way we view Earthquake Detection with an emphasis on how to handle various Architecture and Data Set Issues, along with Real-time Implementation and Ethical Implications. The overall theme of this Chapter is AI in Seismology presents an opportunity to improve Early Warning Systems and help improve Global Seismic Resilience.

title: An EfficientNet-Based Multi-Scale Contextual Attention Network for Robust Mammographic Breast Cancer Analysis
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, making early detection through screening mammography essential. However, the visual variability and low contrast of mammographic lesions continue to challenge reliable interpretation. This paper proposes a deep learning (DL) framework for the automated classification of mammographic images into benign and malignant categories. The proposed model is built upon a pretrained EfficientNetV2-B0 backbone and incorporates two complementary attention mechanisms: a Multi-Scale Squeeze-and-Excitation (MUSE) block to enhance discriminative feature learning across spatial scales, and a Dynamic Non-Local (DNL) block to capture global contextual dependencies among feature channels. Image preprocessing includes contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), intensity normalization, and clinically motivated data augmentation to improve lesion visibility and robustness. The network is trained end-to-end on the MIAS dataset using a lightweight classification head. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements across standard evaluation metrics, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed attention-enhanced architecture for supporting breast cancer screening.

title: PanoWorld: Geometry-Consistent Panoramic Video World Modeling
abstract: We present PanoWorld, a panoramic video world model that generates geometry-consistent 360degree video from a single image and a caption. Existing panoramic video methods optimize primarily for visual realism and do not explicitly constrain the underlying 3D scene state, producing outputs that appear plausible yet exhibit inconsistent depth, broken correspondences, and implausible motion across the spherical surface. We address this gap by framing panoramic video generation as a geometry- and dynamics-consistent latent state modeling problem rather than pure visual synthesis. Building on a pre-trained perspective video world model, we introduce two lightweight regularizers: a depth consistency loss against pseudo ground-truth panoramic depth, and a trajectory consistency loss that supervises the 3D world-frame positions of tracked points across time. We further apply spherical-geometry-aware adaptation to the conditioning and positional encoding. We additionally introduce PanoGeo, a unified geometry-aware panoramic video dataset with consistent depth, trajectory, and prompt annotations across diverse real and synthetic sources, used for both training and stratified evaluation. Experiments show that PanoWorld improves geometric consistency over prior panoramic generation methods while maintaining competitive visual realism, establishing that panoramic video generation must be treated as a geometric modeling problem to support the holistic spatial understanding requirements of embodied AI applications. Code is available at https://github.com/ostadabbas/PanoWorld.

title: From Text to Voice: A Reproducible and Verifiable Framework for Evaluating Tool Calling LLM Agents
abstract: Voice agents increasingly require reliable tool use from speech, whereas prominent tool-calling benchmarks remain text-based. We study whether verified text benchmarks can be converted into controlled audio-based tool calling evaluations without re-annotating the tool schema and gold labels. Our dataset-agnostic framework uses text-to-speech, speaker variation, and environmental noise to create paired text-audio instances while preserving the original dataset annotations. Based on extensive evaluation of 7 omni-modal models on audio-converted versions of Confetti and When2Call, our framework demonstrates that the performance is strongly model- and task-dependent: Gemini-3.1-Flash-Live obtains the highest Confetti score (70.4), whereas GPT-Realtime-1.5 performs best on When2Call (71.9). On Confetti, the text-to-voice gap ranges from 1.8 points for Qwen3-Omni to 4.8 points for GPT-Realtime-1.5. A targeted analysis of failure cases demonstrates that degradations most often reflect misunderstandings of argument values in the speech. Considering real-world deployment scenarios, we further report text-only results, an ambiguity-based reformulation stress test, and a reference-free LLM-as-judge protocol validated against human preferences. Notably, we find that open-source Qwen3 judges with at least 8B parameters exceed 80% agreement with proprietary judges, supporting privacy-preserving evaluation. Overall, our framework provides a verifiable and reproducible first-stage diagnostic that complements purpose-built audio corpora.

title: Privacy Auditing with Zero (0) Training Run
abstract: Privacy auditing provides empirical lower bounds on the differential privacy parameters of learning algorithms. Existing methods, however, require interventional access to the training pipeline, either to retrain models multiple times or to randomize data inclusion. This is often infeasible for large and opaque deployed systems such as foundation or language models. We introduce Zero-Run privacy auditing, a framework for auditing models post-hoc using two fixed datasets: examples known to be training-set members and examples known to be non-members. In this observational regime, membership is no longer randomized; instead, member and non-member data often differ in distribution, so membership inference scores may reflect a distribution shift rather than algorithmic leakage. Drawing on ideas from causal inference, we formalize this confounding effect and propose two complementary corrections that yield valid privacy audits. Our first approach models the combined effect of distribution shift and algorithmic leakage as an adaptive composition, producing conservative global corrections. Our second approach conditions on observed data and adjusts pointwise membership guesses, yielding sharper instance-dependent bounds. Experiments on synthetic data and large-scale image and text models show that Zero-Run auditing enables practical privacy evaluation when retraining or controlled data insertion is infeasible.

title: Ταξινόμηση τουριστικών κριτικών με τεχνικές επεξεργασίας φυσικής γλώσσας: η περίπτωση του Μπάλου
abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξέτασε την αυτόματη ταξινόμηση τουριστικών κριτικών από την πλατφόρμα TripAdvisor, με στόχο την πρόβλεψη της βαθμολογίας που αποδίδει ο επισκέπτης βάσει του κειμένου της κριτικής. Το πεδίο μελέτης ήταν ο τουριστικός προορισμός του Μπάλου στα Χανιά και το σύνολο δεδομένων περιλάμβανε 2.500 κριτικές επισκεπτών. Για την αναπαράσταση των κειμένων εφαρμόστηκαν τεχνικές Επεξεργασίας Φυσικής Γλώσσας, όπως TF-IDF, Word2Vec και BERT. Στη συνέχεια εκπαιδεύτηκαν και συγκρίθηκαν διαφορετικοί ταξινομητές μηχανικής μάθησης, συγκεκριμένα Logistic Regression, SVM, Naive Bayes και Random Forest. Η απόδοση των μοντέλων αξιολογήθηκε μέσω δεικτών όπως Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC και πίνακες σύγχυσης. Συμπληρωματικά, πραγματοποιήθηκε ημι-αυτόματη ανάλυση πτυχών της εμπειρίας των επισκεπτών με χρήση LDA και VADER. Αρχικά, το LDA χρησιμοποιήθηκε για τον εντοπισμό βασικών θεματικών μοτίβων στις κριτικές, τα οποία στη συνέχεια ερμηνεύτηκαν και ομαδοποιήθηκαν σε ευρύτερες πτυχές. Έπειτα, το VADER εφαρμόστηκε για την αποτίμηση του συναισθήματος που σχετίζεται με τις παραπάνω πτυχές. Τα αποτελέσματα ανέδειξαν τη χρησιμότητα των τεχνικών NLP τόσο για την πρόβλεψη της συνολικής αξιολόγησης των επισκεπτών όσο και για την πιο αναλυτική κατανόηση των επιμέρους παραγόντων που διαμορφώνουν την τουριστική εμπειρία στον Μπάλο.

title: Minimax Optimal Sample Complexity for Iterated CVaR Reinforcement Learning With a Generative Model
abstract: Standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms are typically designed to maximize the expected accumulative reward, which may be inadequate in scenarios where risk sensitivity is critical. In this work, the problem of risk-sensitive RL with Iterated Conditional Value at Risk is studied, where the objective is to optimize outcomes under a specified risk level τ at each step. This work provides the first minimax optimal sample complexity analysis for this problem with a generative model. Specifically, the sample complexity is firstly characterized as a function of the number of statesS, actionsA, and effective horizon (1−γ)−1(resp. horizonHin the finite-horizon setting), and is further shown to be minimax optimal via a novel minimax lower bound analysis when the risk level 0Hin the finite horizon setting). For the case when the risk level is small, the limiting case of τ → 0, termed worst-path RL, is then studied, and the minimax optimal sample complexity is also theoretically characterized.

title: Short Text Topic Modeling for Moroccan Darija Online Content: A Comparative Study Between Classical And Embedding-based Approaches
abstract: The study of Moroccan Darija content online is characterized by its considerable dialectic differences and the fact that it suffers from a restricted linguistic resource. The study evaluates classical topic modeling methods, such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), against embedding techniques, such as BERTopic and Top2Vec. An analysis for the corpus is performed over a corpus of over 17,000 records from 10 topic domains covering: health, education, politics, and technology. The insights demonstrate that embedding-based methods are superior to classical methods with respect to topic coherence. Top2Vec achieved an average coherence of 0.64, whereas BERTopic reached 0.47, and consequently produced more interpretable and semantically rich topics. The classical methods yield a moderate coherence score, LDA with an average coherence score of 0.48 and 0.62 for NMF, and poor overall alignment, NMI below 0.25 and ARI below 0.2, with the manual topic labels in all approaches. These research results show that embedding-based models can achieve very efficient topic extraction in sparsely available dialects and can become a useful benchmark for future NLP work in Moroccan Darija.
